svg.aria-label: AWS credential model before the change: the platform stores no AWS credential and assumes a customer-owned role, but the role's trust policy names only the platform account, so it can be assumed on behalf of any tenant.

g.text: AWS — credential model BEFORE
No AWS credential is ever stored, but the customer's role trusts the platform as a whole: nothing in the request says which tenant it is being made for.
CONTROL PLANE (platform)
GITHUB ACTIONS RUN
CUSTOMER AWS ACCOUNT
1 · ONBOARDING (ONCE PER TENANT)
sts:AssumeRole — 15 min, no ExternalId
Operator fills the wizard
account ID, region, role ARN
LLM key, Pinecone key
Encrypts the LLM and Pinecone keys,
generates the docs-signer secret,
then assumes the role and writes all
three into the customer's own account.
Not involved
Onboarding runs inside the platform
itself. CI only enters at deploy time.
IAM role, created by the customer
chatbot-client-deploy-<name>
Trust policy:
Principal = platform AWS account
(no Condition)
Secrets Manager receives the LLM key,
the Pinecone key and the signer secret.
2 · EVERY DEPLOYMENT
Dispatch the workflow
GITHUB_PAT, long-lived
Inputs carry identifiers and ARNs only:
the tenant's keys stay in their account,
so no tenant secret reaches the run.
Nothing in the dispatch states which
tenant the role may be assumed for.
Two hops, both short-lived
1 · GitHub OIDC token
→ platform role (1 h)
2 · role chaining
→ customer role (1 h)
No ExternalId on either hop.
No AWS key is stored in GitHub.
terraform apply
VPC, ALB, ECS services, ECR, S3,
CloudWatch, docs-signer Lambda,
and RDS when pgvector is chosen.
At runtime ECS resolves each secret
by ARN — values never leave the
customer's account.
3 · WHAT THE PLATFORM HOLDS
No AWS credential — but no per-tenant limit on the trust either
Stored: LLM key, Pinecone key and docs-signer secret (AES-256-GCM), plus PLATFORM_ENCRYPTION_KEY and GITHUB_PAT in the environment.
Not stored: any AWS key or session. Access to a customer account exists only for the minutes a role session lasts.
Weakness: the role's trust policy names the platform, not a tenant — anyone who reaches the form and knows a role ARN can have the platform provision into that account.
4 · REVOCATION AND BLAST RADIUS
Revocation
The customer edits or deletes the role. It takes
effect immediately and needs no platform action.
Every AssumeRole call, and everything done with
it, is recorded in the customer's own CloudTrail —
but the record cannot say which tenant it was for.
If the platform database and key are taken
The attacker gains the tenants' LLM, Pinecone and
docs-signer secrets — third-party services and the
upload function, not the AWS accounts themselves.
Reaching an AWS account instead requires the
platform's own identity or its CI.
Compare with fig-21: the same two hops, with a per-tenant sts:ExternalId condition that makes each role assumable for one tenant only.
